input.description: Find project settings dialog run command UI
input.prompt:
In the macOS app at /Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp, find the **project settings dialog/sheet** UI where a project's "run command" is defined/edited.

I need:
1. Exact file path(s) + line numbers of the project settings view (SwiftUI), and how it is presented (sheet? window? Settings scene?).
2. How the run command field is bound — what model/store/Defaults key holds it, the property name, and where it's persisted (config file? Defaults? per-project?).
3. The full layout of the dialog: sections, fields, buttons (Save/Cancel/Done), so I know where a "Run now" button would sit.
4. Any other buttons in that dialog and their styling/idioms (e.g. `.buttonStyle`, label conventions, `.help(...)` tooltips, `.disabled(...)`).

Search breadth: medium. Report file:line references and paste the relevant view body code for the settings dialog. Do not suggest fixes — just locate and report.

input.description: Trace run command execution + running state
input.prompt:
In the macOS app at /Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp, trace the **"run command" execution** machinery.

I need:
1. Where a project's run command is launched from the UI today (menu item? toolbar button? keyboard shortcut? auto-start?). Give file:line for every trigger point and the function/method they call.
2. The state model for "is the run command currently running" — the type, property, and how the UI observes it (e.g. a `@Observable` store, a per-workroom or per-project run session object). Give exact property names and file:line.
3. The public API to start a run (function signature + what arguments it needs — workroom? project? surface?) and to check/query running state for a given project or workroom.
4. Whether run is per-workroom or per-project (i.e. if a project has 3 workrooms, is there one run per workroom?). This matters: I must know what "already running" means and what "Run now" would target.
5. Any existing "disabled if already running" logic in the UI I can mirror.

Search breadth: very thorough. Report file:line references and paste the key signatures/state definitions. Do not suggest fixes — just locate and report.

136	  static func make(_ ref: RootRef) -> Style {
137	    switch ref.kind {
138	    case .branch:
139	      let name = normalized(ref.branch) ?? "root"
140	      return Style(
141	        label: name, tooltip: "Project root · on \(name)",
142	        accessibility: "Project root, on \(name)", ahead: false, dim: false)
143	    case .ancestor:
144	      let name = normalized(ref.branch) ?? "root"
145	      return Style(
146	        label: name, tooltip: "Project root · ahead of \(name)",
147	        accessibility: "Project root, ahead of \(name)", ahead: true, dim: false)
148	    case .detached:
149	      let name = normalized(ref.branch) ?? "detached"
150	      return Style(
151	        label: name, tooltip: "Project root · detached HEAD",
152	        accessibility: "Project root, detached at \(name)", ahead: false, dim: true)
153	    case .none:
154	      return Style(
155	        label: "root", tooltip: "Project root",
156	        accessibility: "Project root", ahead: false, dim: true)
157	    }
158	  }

160	  /// Treats "" / whitespace like nil (the Go side may emit "" rather than null).
161	  private static func normalized(_ s: String?) -> String? {
162	    guard let s, !s.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespaces).isEmpty else { return nil }
163	    return s
164	  }

questions.question: Run is per-TARGET (a workroom or the project root), but the settings sheet is per-project. Which target should "Run now" act on?

options.label: Origin target, else selection, else root (Recommended)
options.description: Carry a `runTarget` on `PendingProjectSettings`. The ⌘R/no-command path passes the exact target that failed to run (issue #127 flow). The sidebar gear/context-menu paths pass the current selection if it belongs to this project, else `project.rootTarget`. Tooltip names the target so it's never ambiguous.

options.label: Always the project root
options.description: Run now always runs in the project directory itself, never a workroom. Simple and unambiguous, but breaks the motivating flow: ⌘R on workroom X with no command, set one, Run now — would run in the root, not X.
options.preview:
// no model change needed
store.runOrFocusRunCommand(for: project.rootTarget)

options.label: Only when a target is known
options.description: Show Run now only for the ⌘R/no-command entry (which knows the target). The plain "Project Settings…" gear/context-menu entry never shows it, even with a command defined.

questions.question: The sheet uses a draft + Save model — the field isn't persisted until Save, and `startRunCommand` reads the persisted config. What should "Run now" do with unsaved edits?

options.label: Save, run, dismiss (Recommended)
options.description: Run now = commit the draft, start the run, close the sheet. Makes the issue-#127 flow one click (type command → Run now) instead of Save → ⌘R. Label stays "Run now"; tooltip spells out that it saves.
options.preview:
Button("Run now") {
  store.setRunConfig(RunConfig(command: command, autoRun: autoRun),
                     forProject: project.path)
  store.runOrFocusRunCommand(for: target)
  dismiss()
}
.disabled(store.isRunCommandRunning(for: target.id))
.help("Save and run in \(target.title)")

options.label: Label it "Save & Run"
options.description: Same behaviour, but the label states the save outright. Longer footer row; three commit-ish buttons (Save & Run / Cancel / Save) read heavier.

options.label: Run persisted command only
options.description: Run now runs what's already saved and is disabled while the field differs from it. Never surprises you by persisting, but the ⌘R-with-no-command flow still needs Save first, so the button is dead exactly when it'd help most.

questions.question: Where should the button sit in the sheet's footer row?

options.label: Leading edge (Recommended)
options.description: macOS convention: auxiliary action at the leading edge, dismiss buttons trailing. Keeps Cancel/Save adjacent as today.

options.label: Next to Save
options.description: Groups all three actions at the trailing edge. Puts Cancel between two commit actions.

options.label: Inside the Form section
options.description: A row under the auto-run toggle, inside the grouped form — reads as part of the Run Command section rather than a sheet-level action.
